answer_choices: High-sensitivity cardiac troponin
Exercise treadmill stress test
CT coronary angiography
D-dimer
Upper gastrointestinal endoscopy
packages.author_rationale: Suspected acute coronary syndrome is classified from the ischaemic clinical presentation together with the electrocardiogram and cardiac troponin, so troponin is the investigation that completes the initial diagnostic triad in this patient. A single non-diagnostic electrocardiogram does not exclude acute coronary syndrome: when suspicion persists, the electrocardiogram and high-sensitivity troponin are repeated at the assay-specific interval rather than treated as definitive. The learner should recognise that exertional central chest pressure with diaphoresis in a patient with cardiac risk factors is an ischaemic presentation, and that a normal initial tracing raises rather than lowers the importance of measuring troponin. The learner should also recognise that a troponin value is interpreted in the ischaemic clinical context and does not by itself establish myocardial infarction.

packages.conditional_next_action_information: If the initial electrocardiogram had shown diagnostic ST-segment elevation, the decision would shift from measuring a biomarker to arranging reperfusion without waiting for troponin. If suspicion persists after this first non-diagnostic electrocardiogram and first troponin, both are repeated at the assay-specific interval rather than accepted as definitive.
packages.lead_in: In addition to the electrocardiogram, which investigation is most important to obtain now?

per_distractor_rationales.choice: Exercise treadmill stress test
per_distractor_rationales.what_would_make_correct: It becomes a reasonable choice for a patient whose acute coronary syndrome has already been excluded and who is being assessed electively for stable exertional angina.
per_distractor_rationales.why_inferior_here: Acute coronary syndrome has not yet been excluded in this patient, and the initial classification depends on the presentation, the electrocardiogram and troponin rather than on provocative testing.
per_distractor_rationales.why_plausible: Provocative testing is a recognised route to diagnosing ischaemic heart disease, and the pain was brought on by exertion, which invites a functional test.

per_distractor_rationales.choice: CT coronary angiography
per_distractor_rationales.what_would_make_correct: It becomes appropriate once the acute syndrome has been addressed and a specific diagnostic question about coronary anatomy remains after initial assessment.
per_distractor_rationales.why_inferior_here: Anatomical coronary imaging is a downstream test selected according to risk and the remaining clinical question; it does not replace the troponin needed to classify the acute presentation now.
per_distractor_rationales.why_plausible: Coronary imaging directly visualises the coronary arteries and is increasingly used in chest-pain pathways.

per_distractor_rationales.choice: D-dimer
per_distractor_rationales.what_would_make_correct: It becomes the right next test when the history and risk factors generate a low or moderate pretest probability of pulmonary embolism.
per_distractor_rationales.why_inferior_here: Suspected pulmonary embolism is evaluated from pretest probability, and this presentation, exertional central pressure with radiation and diaphoresis, without sudden dyspnoea, pleuritic pain, hypoxaemia or venous thromboembolism risk factors, does not generate that pretest probability.
per_distractor_rationales.why_plausible: Pulmonary embolism is an important alternative cause of acute chest pain and D-dimer is part of its assessment.

per_distractor_rationales.choice: Upper gastrointestinal endoscopy
per_distractor_rationales.what_would_make_correct: It becomes appropriate after adequate cardiac evaluation in a patient whose symptoms point to reflux and in whom objective confirmation is required.
per_distractor_rationales.why_inferior_here: Chest pain without typical reflux symptoms should receive an adequate cardiac evaluation before objective testing is used to establish gastro-oesophageal reflux disease.
per_distractor_rationales.why_plausible: Reflux disease commonly causes chest discomfort and is a frequent alternative explanation in chest-pain clinics.

packages.stem: A 58-year-old man presents to the emergency department after 45 minutes of central chest pressure radiating to the left arm, accompanied by sweating and nausea. The discomfort began while he was walking uphill and settled about 20 minutes before arrival. He has hypertension and smokes. He is comfortable at rest. Heart rate is 78 beats/min, blood pressure 142/86 mmHg, respiratory rate 16 breaths/min, oxygen saturation 97% on room air. Cardiac and respiratory examination is unremarkable, the chest wall is not tender, and there is no leg swelling. A 12-lead electrocardiogram shows sinus rhythm with no ST-segment or T-wave abnormality.

answer_choices: Fitness to drive is judged on his symptoms and his response to treatment rather than on the severity score alone, and the provincial licensing authority makes any restriction decision; in the meantime he should avoid alcohol and sedating sleep aids before bed and work on weight, smoking and regular sleep timing.

The apnea-hypopnea index recorded on his sleep study determines by itself whether he is permitted to drive, irrespective of how sleepy he feels, whether he has had a near-miss, or how well he responds to treatment.
Losing weight and sleeping on his side will cure his obstructive sleep apnea, so once he has made those two changes he will need no device, no prescription, and no further sleep-medicine follow-up.

A drink in the evening or his over-the-counter sleep aid will deepen his sleep and so reduce his daytime sleepiness, and he can go on using either of them while he waits for his treatment to be arranged.
Because he holds a private rather than a commercial licence, no driving restriction can ever apply to him and the provincial licensing authority has no role in a case like his.
packages.author_proposed_key: Fitness to drive is judged on his symptoms and his response to treatment rather than on the severity score alone, and the provincial licensing authority makes any restriction decision; in the meantime he should avoid alcohol and sedating sleep aids before bed and work on weight, smoking and regular sleep timing.
packages.author_rationale: Two things are decisive. First, in obstructive sleep apnea, clinical fitness-to-drive assessment turns on symptoms and treatment response rather than on the severity index alone, and the decision to restrict a licence rests with the provincial licensing authority, not with the physician alone. Second, the modifiable risks that can be addressed immediately are weight, physical activity, smoking, regular sleep timing, side sleeping where appropriate, and avoidance of alcohol and sedating medication before sleep. The learner should recognise that these two strands, a jurisdictional safety duty and an individualised risk-reduction plan, belong in the same conversation, and that lifestyle advice is offered alongside confirmed diagnosis and individualised treatment rather than in place of them.

Canadian Thoracic Society and Canadian Sleep Society

packages.conditional_next_action_information: If he drove a commercial vehicle, the fitness assessment would be more stringent, and provincial requirements would still govern implementation. The specific reporting obligation and any interim restriction are set by the province in which he is licensed.
packages.lead_in: Which counselling statement is most appropriate?
packages.learner_decision: Counsel on safety and modifiable risks.

per_distractor_rationales.choice: The apnea-hypopnea index recorded on his sleep study determines by itself whether he is permitted to drive, irrespective of how sleepy he feels, whether he has had a near-miss, or how well he responds to treatment.
per_distractor_rationales.what_would_make_correct: Nothing in this scenario; it would require guidance that made the severity index the sole determinant of driving fitness.
per_distractor_rationales.why_inferior_here: Canadian guidance directs that fitness assessment consider symptoms and treatment response rather than sleep apnea severity alone, so a score-only rule misstates the basis of the decision.
per_distractor_rationales.why_plausible: A single numerical index is an appealingly objective basis for a safety decision, and severity thresholds are widely quoted.

per_distractor_rationales.choice: Losing weight and sleeping on his side will cure his obstructive sleep apnea, so once he has made those two changes he will need no device, no prescription, and no further sleep-medicine follow-up.
per_distractor_rationales.what_would_make_correct: The lifestyle content would be correct if offered as risk reduction alongside confirmed diagnosis, individualised treatment and follow-up rather than as a cure that replaces them.
per_distractor_rationales.why_inferior_here: The same guidance directs that the diagnosis be confirmed and treatment individualised rather than presenting lifestyle change as universal definitive therapy, so promising a cure and discharging follow-up is wrong.
per_distractor_rationales.why_plausible: Weight management and positional measures are genuine components of the advice given to patients with obstructive sleep apnea.

per_distractor_rationales.choice: A drink in the evening or his over-the-counter sleep aid will deepen his sleep and so reduce his daytime sleepiness, and he can go on using either of them while he waits for his treatment to be arranged.
per_distractor_rationales.what_would_make_correct: Nothing in this scenario; avoiding these agents before sleep is itself part of the modifiable-risk advice.
per_distractor_rationales.why_inferior_here: Alcohol and sedating sleep or pain medicines can worsen airway obstruction and prolong apneic pauses, and must not be framed as treatment for sleep apnea; this advice would increase rather than reduce his risk.
per_distractor_rationales.why_plausible: Patients commonly experience alcohol and sedatives as helping them fall asleep, and he is already using both.

per_distractor_rationales.choice: Because he holds a private rather than a commercial licence, no driving restriction can ever apply to him and the provincial licensing authority has no role in a case like his.
per_distractor_rationales.what_would_make_correct: Nothing in this scenario; the commercial-versus-private distinction changes the stringency of assessment, not whether the licensing authority is involved.
per_distractor_rationales.why_inferior_here: Commercial assessment is more stringent, but licensing authorities make restriction decisions under provincial rules for non-commercial drivers as well, so telling him the authority has no role is incorrect and unsafe given his near-miss.
per_distractor_rationales.why_plausible: Fitness standards are more stringent for commercial drivers, which can suggest that private drivers are unaffected.

packages.stem: A 48-year-old man in Ontario has just been diagnosed with obstructive sleep apnea. He reports loud snoring, witnessed apneas and marked daytime sleepiness, and describes drifting across a lane on the highway last month before a passenger woke him. He holds a standard non-commercial driver's licence and does not drive for work. He drinks two or three alcoholic drinks in the evening most nights, takes an over-the-counter sleep aid, smokes, and has gained 12 kg over five years. He asks whether he is allowed to drive and what he can do himself while treatment is being arranged.

answer_choices: Supportive care with attention to feeding and hydration and repeated clinical assessment, without routine bronchodilators or corticosteroids
Regular nebulised salbutamol every four hours, continued while the wheeze persists
A single dose of oral dexamethasone, given now to reduce her airway inflammation
A seven-day course of oral amoxicillin, started now to cover a bacterial chest infection
Supplemental oxygen by nasal cannula, started now and continued until her wheeze settles
packages.author_proposed_key: Supportive care with attention to feeding and hydration and repeated clinical assessment, without routine bronchodilators or corticosteroids
packages.author_rationale: This is typical bronchiolitis in an infant under two years: a first wheezing episode following two to three days of coryzal symptoms, progressing to tachypnoea, wheeze and crackles with mild distress, and it is diagnosed clinically. Management is supportive. Routine salbutamol, corticosteroids and antibiotics are not recommended, and repeated clinical assessment by staff competent in paediatric respiratory assessment is the central element of monitoring. The learner should recognise the syndrome from its age and course, and should recognise that the absence of a disease-modifying drug treatment is the expected answer rather than an omission.
packages.conditional_next_action_information: If the diagnosis were unclear, the course unexpectedly poor, or the severity raised concern for an alternative such as bacterial pneumonia, chest radiography would then be considered; it is not part of routine assessment in typical bronchiolitis. A sustained saturation below 90% would add supplemental oxygen, and inability to feed safely would change the feeding plan.
packages.lead_in: Which is the most appropriate management?
packages.learner_decision: Recognize that management of typical bronchiolitis is primarily supportive.

per_distractor_rationales.choice: Regular nebulised salbutamol every four hours, continued while the wheeze persists
per_distractor_rationales.what_would_make_correct: It becomes appropriate for a child whose presentation indicates asthma rather than typical bronchiolitis, such as recurrent episodes with a documented bronchodilator response.
per_distractor_rationales.why_inferior_here: Routine salbutamol is not recommended in bronchiolitis; the wheeze here arises from small-airway inflammation and secretions in a first episode in an infant, not from the reversible bronchospasm that bronchodilators target.
per_distractor_rationales.why_plausible: Wheeze is the dominant physical finding, and bronchodilators are the reflex response to wheeze in older children with asthma.

per_distractor_rationales.choice: A single dose of oral dexamethasone, given now to reduce her airway inflammation
per_distractor_rationales.what_would_make_correct: It becomes appropriate for a different diagnosis with an established steroid indication, such as croup or an asthma exacerbation.
per_distractor_rationales.why_inferior_here: Routine corticosteroids are not recommended in bronchiolitis, and this infant has no separate indication for them.
per_distractor_rationales.why_plausible: Corticosteroids are effective in several paediatric respiratory illnesses that also cause noisy breathing and distress.

per_distractor_rationales.choice: A seven-day course of oral amoxicillin, started now to cover a bacterial chest infection
per_distractor_rationales.what_would_make_correct: It becomes appropriate when a bacterial infection is separately indicated, for example a focal consolidation or another identified bacterial source.
per_distractor_rationales.why_inferior_here: Routine antibiotics are not recommended in bronchiolitis unless another indication is present, and her findings are diffuse and bilateral rather than focal.
per_distractor_rationales.why_plausible: The infant is febrile with an abnormal chest examination, which can suggest bacterial pneumonia.

per_distractor_rationales.choice: Supplemental oxygen by nasal cannula, started now and continued until her wheeze settles
per_distractor_rationales.what_would_make_correct: It becomes correct if her saturation fell and remained below 90%, when oxygen would be given and titrated to at least 90%.
per_distractor_rationales.why_inferior_here: Supplemental oxygen is given when the saturation remains below 90%, and this infant is maintaining 94% on room air, so oxygen is not the management this presentation calls for.
per_distractor_rationales.why_plausible: Oxygen is a genuine part of supportive care in bronchiolitis and the infant has increased work of breathing.

packages.stem: A previously healthy 7-month-old infant is brought to the emergency department in February. Three days of clear rhinorrhoea, cough and low-grade fever have been followed today by noisy breathing. This is her first episode of wheezing. She is alert and consolable. Temperature is 37.8 degrees Celsius, respiratory rate 52 breaths/min, heart rate 140 beats/min, oxygen saturation 94% on room air. There is mild subcostal indrawing, and the chest has widespread wheeze and fine crackles without focal findings. She has taken about three-quarters of her usual feed volumes and has had four wet nappies in the past day.

answer_choices: Untreated severe hyperbilirubinaemia can injure the brain, and the decision to treat depends on the measured bilirubin interpreted against the infant's age in hours, gestational age and neurotoxicity risk factors
The bilirubin level is the test that confirms biliary atresia, and it is needed today because surgical referral for that condition is time-critical
The bilirubin level determines whether breastfeeding must be stopped permanently, and the decision has to be made before the milk supply is established
The bilirubin level is the test used to diagnose neonatal sepsis, and sepsis must be identified today in a newborn who is feeding poorly and is hard to rouse
Jaundice at this age is always physiological and resolves without treatment, so the measurement is taken only to document the visit rather than to change what is done
packages.author_proposed_key: Untreated severe hyperbilirubinaemia can injure the brain, and the decision to treat depends on the measured bilirubin interpreted against the infant's age in hours, gestational age and neurotoxicity risk factors
packages.author_rationale: Clinically apparent or suspected significant jaundice in a newborn requires prompt measurement of total serum or transcutaneous bilirubin, because the reason for measuring is the risk of bilirubin-induced neurological injury, and because treatment and follow-up are decided by comparing the measured value against an hour-specific threshold modified by gestational age and neurotoxicity risk. The learner should recognise that visible jaundice extending over the trunk and limbs in a poorly feeding newborn with significant weight loss is a presentation that demands a number today, and that the number is meaningless without the age in hours and risk context against which it is read.

canadian_source_refs.date_or_version: Guidelines for detection and management of hyperbilirubinemia in term and late preterm newborns
canadian_source_refs.locator: Clinical assessment; bilirubin measurement; treatment thresholds

packages.conditional_next_action_information: The measured value is interpreted against age in hours, gestational age and neurotoxicity risk factors to decide between phototherapy, escalation, or timed repeat measurement and follow-up. This item deliberately does not turn on any specific numerical treatment threshold, which is read from the applicable nomogram.
packages.lead_in: Which explanation best states why the bilirubin must be measured without delay?
packages.learner_decision: Recognize kernicterus as the feared complication of untreated severe hyperbilirubinemia.

per_distractor_rationales.choice: The bilirubin level is the test that confirms biliary atresia, and it is needed today because surgical referral for that condition is time-critical
per_distractor_rationales.what_would_make_correct: Cholestatic jaundice becomes the concern when jaundice persists beyond the early weeks or when the conjugated fraction is raised, which is investigated differently.
per_distractor_rationales.why_inferior_here: A total bilirubin value does not establish biliary atresia, and it is not the reason this measurement is urgent on day five; the urgency here is the neurotoxicity risk of a high unconjugated bilirubin and the threshold-based treatment decision.
per_distractor_rationales.why_plausible: Biliary atresia is a genuine and time-critical cause of neonatal jaundice, and delayed referral harms outcomes.

per_distractor_rationales.choice: The bilirubin level determines whether breastfeeding must be stopped permanently, and the decision has to be made before the milk supply is established
per_distractor_rationales.what_would_make_correct: Nothing in this scenario; feeding support is part of management rather than something the bilirubin value is used to terminate.
per_distractor_rationales.why_inferior_here: The measurement guides threshold-based treatment and follow-up, not a decision to stop breastfeeding permanently, so this misstates both the purpose of the test and the management that follows it.
per_distractor_rationales.why_plausible: Jaundice is common in exclusively breastfed newborns and parents are often told feeding is implicated.

per_distractor_rationales.choice: The bilirubin level is the test used to diagnose neonatal sepsis, and sepsis must be identified today in a newborn who is feeding poorly and is hard to rouse
per_distractor_rationales.what_would_make_correct: Suspected sepsis is assessed and investigated on its own pathway; it would not convert bilirubin into the diagnostic test for it.
per_distractor_rationales.why_inferior_here: Bilirubin is not a diagnostic test for sepsis; it is being measured here because the height of the bilirubin itself, read against age and risk, determines whether treatment is needed to prevent neurological injury.
per_distractor_rationales.why_plausible: A lethargic, poorly feeding newborn does raise concern for sepsis, and jaundice can accompany it.

per_distractor_rationales.choice: Jaundice at this age is always physiological and resolves without treatment, so the measurement is taken only to document the visit rather than to change what is done
per_distractor_rationales.what_would_make_correct: Nothing in this scenario; the commonness of physiological jaundice is the reason thresholds exist, not a reason to omit the measurement.
per_distractor_rationales.why_inferior_here: Clinically apparent significant jaundice requires prompt measurement precisely because visual estimation cannot separate benign from treatment-threshold hyperbilirubinaemia, and this infant also has poor feeding and 9% weight loss.
per_distractor_rationales.why_plausible: Most neonatal jaundice is benign and self-limiting, which can make same-day measurement feel excessive.

packages.stem: A term newborn is brought to the clinic on day five of life because she is feeding poorly and is difficult to rouse for feeds. She is exclusively breastfed and has lost 9% of her birth weight. She is afebrile and her vital signs are normal. She is visibly jaundiced over the face, chest, abdomen and thighs. The physician arranges immediate measurement of the bilirubin, and the parents ask why a blood test is needed today rather than at the scheduled visit next week.

answer_choices: Admit for haemodynamic stabilisation with intravenous access and fluid resuscitation, urgent haemoglobin measurement with treatment of severe anaemia, and treatment directed at controlling the bleeding
Prescribe tranexamic acid and arrange review at or shortly after her next period
Prescribe a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug and arrange review in three months
Arrange insertion of a levonorgestrel intrauterine system at the next available outpatient appointment
Arrange an outpatient endometrial biopsy before any treatment is started
packages.author_proposed_key: Admit for haemodynamic stabilisation with intravenous access and fluid resuscitation, urgent haemoglobin measurement with treatment of severe anaemia, and treatment directed at controlling the bleeding
packages.author_rationale: The decisive feature is that this is acute uncontrolled heavy bleeding with haemodynamic compromise, not heavy menstrual bleeding in a stable patient. Tachycardia, hypotension with postural symptoms, pallor and an hourly soaked pad over six hours define a presentation that requires prompt stabilisation and bleeding control together with rapid assessment and treatment of severe anaemia. The learner should recognise that the severity of the bleeding, rather than its underlying cause, sets the tempo of management, and that the structured diagnostic workup for abnormal uterine bleeding, including excluding pregnancy and classifying structural and non-structural causes, proceeds alongside and after stabilisation rather than before it.

canadian_source_refs.organization: Society of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists of Canada

canadian_source_refs.locator: Quality Statement 8: Acute Heavy Menstrual Bleeding, pages 23–24

packages.conditional_next_action_information: Had she been haemodynamically stable, management would move to the shared-choice pathway among non-hormonal and hormonal options matched to contraindications and goals, with follow-up at or immediately after the next period. A positive pregnancy test would move her onto an entirely different pathway.
packages.lead_in: Which is the most appropriate immediate management?
packages.learner_decision: Recognize when bleeding severity requires urgent intervention.

per_distractor_rationales.choice: Prescribe tranexamic acid and arrange review at or shortly after her next period
per_distractor_rationales.what_would_make_correct: It becomes appropriate once she is stabilised, or for a woman with heavy periods who is haemodynamically stable and choosing among non-hormonal and hormonal options.
per_distractor_rationales.why_inferior_here: That shared-choice outpatient pathway is for stable heavy menstrual bleeding; this patient is haemodynamically unstable, so discharging her on an oral agent leaves the immediate threat untreated.
per_distractor_rationales.why_plausible: Tranexamic acid is a genuine first-line non-hormonal treatment for heavy menstrual bleeding and review after the next period is the standard follow-up interval.

per_distractor_rationales.choice: Prescribe a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug and arrange review in three months
per_distractor_rationales.what_would_make_correct: It becomes reasonable for a stable woman whose goal is reduced menstrual loss and who has chosen a non-hormonal option.
per_distractor_rationales.why_inferior_here: This is again the stable-patient pathway, and a three-month horizon is incompatible with a patient who is hypotensive and actively bleeding now.
per_distractor_rationales.why_plausible: Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs are an accepted non-hormonal option for heavy menstrual bleeding and a three-month review is a common outpatient interval.

per_distractor_rationales.choice: Arrange insertion of a levonorgestrel intrauterine system at the next available outpatient appointment
per_distractor_rationales.what_would_make_correct: It becomes appropriate as a longer-term plan after stabilisation, when the patient is choosing among hormonal options matched to her contraindications and goals.
per_distractor_rationales.why_inferior_here: It is an elective outpatient treatment within the stable-patient shared-choice pathway and does nothing for the acute haemodynamic compromise in front of the clinician.
per_distractor_rationales.why_plausible: The levonorgestrel intrauterine system is a highly effective long-term treatment for heavy menstrual bleeding and is often the preferred option.

per_distractor_rationales.choice: Arrange an outpatient endometrial biopsy before any treatment is started
per_distractor_rationales.what_would_make_correct: It becomes indicated in a patient with those risk factors, as part of assessment rather than as a precondition for urgent treatment.
per_distractor_rationales.why_inferior_here: Endometrial sampling is reserved for patients carrying risk factors for hyperplasia or endometrial malignancy, such as being older than 40, having anovulatory cycles, ongoing bleeding between periods, obesity, diabetes, or a long history of oestrogen exposure unopposed by a progestogen. None of these is described here, and making a biopsy a precondition for treatment would delay her stabilisation.
per_distractor_rationales.why_plausible: Endometrial sampling is an important part of evaluating abnormal uterine bleeding and it feels prudent to obtain tissue before treating.

packages.stem: A 27-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with heavy menstrual bleeding. Her periods have been heavy for about a year, but today she has soaked through a pad every hour for the past six hours and has passed large clots. She feels light-headed on standing. Heart rate is 118 beats/min, blood pressure 88/54 mmHg lying and lower on standing, and she is pale with cool peripheries. A urine pregnancy test is negative. Abdominal examination is soft and non-tender; on speculum examination there is active bleeding from the cervical os and no cervical or vaginal lesion.

answer_choices: Blood group and antibody screen
Group B streptococcus vaginal-rectal swab
Glucose challenge test for gestational diabetes
Fetal fibronectin swab
packages.author_rationale: The initial prenatal assessment has a defined baseline laboratory panel offered to everyone: complete blood count, blood group and antibody screen, rubella immunity, syphilis, hepatitis B and HIV testing, with further infection and genetic screening determined by provincial guidance and individual risk. Blood group and antibody screen is the only listed option that belongs to that panel. The learner should recognise that prenatal investigations are staged across pregnancy and that a test being routine in pregnancy does not make it part of the first-visit baseline panel.

canadian_source_refs.date_or_version: Care during pregnancy: Family-centred maternity and newborn care national guidelines
canadian_source_refs.locator: Initial visit and Appendix B laboratory screening

packages.conditional_next_action_information: Which further infection and genetic screening is offered, and when, is determined by provincial guidance and by the patient's individual risk; the baseline panel itself is the component that is offered to everyone at the initial visit.
packages.lead_in: Which investigation belongs to that routine baseline panel?
packages.learner_decision: Interpret the components of an initial prenatal visit, including baseline history, physical exam, and first-trimester investigations.

per_distractor_rationales.choice: Group B streptococcus vaginal-rectal swab
per_distractor_rationales.what_would_make_correct: It becomes the right answer for a visit in the late third trimester at which screening for intrapartum prophylaxis is arranged.
per_distractor_rationales.why_inferior_here: It is a later-pregnancy screen whose purpose is to guide intrapartum prophylaxis, and it is not one of the baseline investigations that make up the initial-visit panel.
per_distractor_rationales.why_plausible: Group B streptococcus screening is a routine part of Canadian prenatal care and is offered to essentially every pregnant patient.

per_distractor_rationales.choice: Glucose challenge test for gestational diabetes
per_distractor_rationales.what_would_make_correct: It becomes the right answer at the second-trimester visit at which gestational diabetes screening is arranged, or earlier when individual risk prompts earlier testing.
per_distractor_rationales.why_inferior_here: It is a second-trimester screen for a condition that develops as pregnancy advances, and it is not part of the first-visit baseline panel.
per_distractor_rationales.why_plausible: Screening for gestational diabetes is routine in Canadian prenatal care and the glucose challenge test is its usual first step, so it is familiar as a test that essentially every pregnant patient has.

per_distractor_rationales.choice: Fetal fibronectin swab
per_distractor_rationales.what_would_make_correct: It becomes relevant only when a patient presents later in pregnancy with symptoms raising concern for preterm labour.
per_distractor_rationales.why_inferior_here: It is used to assess the risk of imminent preterm birth in a symptomatic patient, not as a baseline screen in an asymptomatic first-trimester patient, and it does not appear in the initial-visit panel.
per_distractor_rationales.why_plausible: It is a recognised obstetric test and its name suggests a general assessment of the pregnancy.

packages.stem: A 26-year-old woman in her first pregnancy attends her family physician for her initial prenatal visit in the first trimester. She is well, takes no medication other than a folic-acid-containing prenatal vitamin, and has no personal or family history of note. A baseline history is taken and a physical examination performed, and the physician then orders the routine baseline laboratory panel offered to all pregnant patients at this visit.

answer_choices: Menopausal hormone therapy, after reviewing her individual contraindications and the balance of benefits and risks with her
Compounded bioidentical hormone preparations prepared by a compounding pharmacy
Lifestyle measures alone, with review in one year
A non-hormonal prescription alternative, because hormone therapy is contraindicated once menopause has occurred
Deferring all treatment until a further year of amenorrhoea has passed
packages.author_proposed_key: Menopausal hormone therapy, after reviewing her individual contraindications and the balance of benefits and risks with her
packages.author_rationale: For bothersome vasomotor symptoms, menopausal hormone therapy is the first-line treatment when an individualised assessment finds no contraindication and the benefits outweigh the risks for that person. Both halves matter: the recommendation is conditional on the individualised assessment, and this patient's history and examination are precisely what that assessment reviews. The learner should recognise that symptom burden, not the mere fact of menopause, drives treatment, and that the counselling task is to pair the first-line option with an explicit contraindication and risk-benefit review rather than to offer the drug unconditionally or to withhold it by rule.

canadian_source_refs.locator: Quality statement: treatment for vasomotor symptoms
canadian_source_refs.organization: Menopause: Care for People 40 Years of Age or Older

packages.conditional_next_action_information: If the individualised review identified a contraindication, or if she preferred to avoid hormone therapy, the discussion would move to non-hormonal options. The route, formulation and need for progestogen depend on her uterine status and are part of the same individualised assessment.
packages.lead_in: Which is the most appropriate first-line option to discuss with her?
packages.learner_decision: Counsel on prevention and management of the undesirable effects of menopause.

per_distractor_rationales.choice: Compounded bioidentical hormone preparations prepared by a compounding pharmacy
per_distractor_rationales.what_would_make_correct: Nothing in this scenario; a patient's preference for such a product is a reason for discussion, not a reason to make it the first-line recommendation.
per_distractor_rationales.why_inferior_here: The first-line recommendation is for menopausal hormone therapy assessed and prescribed in the regulated way described above; a compounded preparation is not that therapy and substituting it abandons the evidence base the recommendation rests on.
per_distractor_rationales.why_plausible: Patients frequently ask for these preparations and the word bioidentical suggests a gentler or more natural version of the same treatment.

per_distractor_rationales.choice: Lifestyle measures alone, with review in one year
per_distractor_rationales.what_would_make_correct: It becomes reasonable for mild symptoms that are not bothersome, or as an adjunct alongside a first-line treatment.
per_distractor_rationales.why_inferior_here: Her symptoms are frequent and function-limiting, and for bothersome vasomotor symptoms hormone therapy is the first-line treatment in the absence of contraindication; offering lifestyle measures alone with a one-year horizon under-treats her.
per_distractor_rationales.why_plausible: Lifestyle advice is safe, universally applicable and a reasonable adjunct for many menopausal symptoms.

per_distractor_rationales.choice: A non-hormonal prescription alternative, because hormone therapy is contraindicated once menopause has occurred
per_distractor_rationales.what_would_make_correct: A non-hormonal option becomes appropriate when the individualised assessment identifies a contraindication to hormone therapy or when the patient prefers to avoid it.
per_distractor_rationales.why_inferior_here: The stated reason is wrong: being postmenopausal is not itself a contraindication to hormone therapy, and the recommendation turns on an individualised contraindication and risk-benefit assessment, which this patient passes.
per_distractor_rationales.why_plausible: Non-hormonal prescription options do exist for vasomotor symptoms and are genuinely used, which makes the option look familiar.

per_distractor_rationales.choice: Deferring all treatment until a further year of amenorrhoea has passed
per_distractor_rationales.what_would_make_correct: Nothing in this scenario; unexplained bleeding or diagnostic uncertainty would prompt investigation rather than a fixed waiting period.
per_distractor_rationales.why_inferior_here: No such deferral rule governs treatment; bothersome vasomotor symptoms are treated on their symptom burden after individualised assessment, and withholding treatment for a further year serves no diagnostic purpose in a woman who is already well past the point at which menopause is established.
per_distractor_rationales.why_plausible: Menopause is defined by a period of amenorrhoea, so a waiting rule sounds like sound diagnostic discipline.

packages.stem: A 52-year-old woman attends her family physician. Her last menstrual period was 14 months ago. For the past year she has had eight to ten hot flushes a day and drenching night sweats that wake her repeatedly, and she is exhausted and struggling at work. She has no history of breast cancer, venous thromboembolism, coronary artery disease, stroke, liver disease or unexplained vaginal bleeding, and there is no family history of breast cancer. Blood pressure is 118/74 mmHg and body mass index is 24 kg/m2. She takes no medication. She asks what will most reliably relieve her symptoms.

answer_choices: Non-contrast CT of the head
MRI of the brain
Skull radiographs
CT angiography of the head and neck
No imaging, with clinical observation and reassessment in six hours
packages.author_rationale: Canadian radiology referral guidance places acute head injury with a suspicion of intracranial damage in the CT pathway, and this presentation raises exactly that suspicion: witnessed loss of consciousness, a persistently depressed and confused level of consciousness, a scalp haematoma from a fall down stairs, and anticoagulation. The learner should recognise that the question being asked of imaging is whether there is acute intracranial blood, and that CT is the modality selected for that question in the acute traumatic setting, where it is fast, widely available and sensitive to fresh haemorrhage.

canadian_source_refs.organization: Canadian Association of Radiologists Trauma Referral Guidelines
Canadian Association of Radiologists Spine Referral Guidelines

packages.conditional_next_action_information: Anticoagulation raises the concern for intracranial haemorrhage and does not change the modality; if the scan shows haemorrhage, reversal and neurosurgical consultation follow. This item does not turn on any specific decision-rule threshold for imaging after head injury.
packages.lead_in: Which imaging investigation is most appropriate now?
packages.learner_decision: Select CT as the first-line imaging modality for acute head trauma with concern for intracranial injury.

per_distractor_rationales.choice: MRI of the brain
per_distractor_rationales.what_would_make_correct: It becomes the right modality for the non-traumatic or subacute neurological questions that referral guidance assigns to MRI.
per_distractor_rationales.why_inferior_here: The same referral guidance points MRI at a different set of questions, such as non-traumatic acute-onset or progressive myelopathy, while a head injury with suspected intracranial damage belongs in the CT pathway; MRI would also be slower in a patient who may need urgent neurosurgical decisions.
per_distractor_rationales.why_plausible: MRI gives superior soft-tissue detail and detects lesions CT can miss, which makes it look like the more thorough choice.

per_distractor_rationales.choice: Skull radiographs
per_distractor_rationales.what_would_make_correct: Nothing in this scenario; radiographs do not address the intracranial question that his presentation raises.
per_distractor_rationales.why_inferior_here: The clinical question is whether there is intracranial injury, which radiographs cannot answer; referral guidance places that question in the CT pathway, and a normal film would not exclude intracranial haemorrhage.
per_distractor_rationales.why_plausible: A radiograph is quick and cheap, and a skull fracture is a genuine concern after a fall onto the head.

per_distractor_rationales.choice: CT angiography of the head and neck
per_distractor_rationales.what_would_make_correct: It becomes appropriate when the assessment raises a specific concern for arterial injury, such as suspected blunt cerebrovascular injury, usually after the non-contrast study.
per_distractor_rationales.why_inferior_here: It answers a vascular question rather than the immediate question of acute intracranial haemorrhage, and it is not the first study chosen for a head injury with suspected intracranial damage.
per_distractor_rationales.why_plausible: It is a CT-based study and vascular injury can accompany head and neck trauma.

per_distractor_rationales.choice: No imaging, with clinical observation and reassessment in six hours
per_distractor_rationales.what_would_make_correct: It becomes reasonable for a fully alert patient after a minor mechanism whose assessment raises no suspicion of intracranial damage.
per_distractor_rationales.why_inferior_here: Observation without imaging is not appropriate once the presentation has raised a suspicion of intracranial damage; deferring the scan in a drowsy, confused, anticoagulated patient risks missing a haemorrhage during the observation period.
per_distractor_rationales.why_plausible: Many minor head injuries are managed with observation, and avoiding radiation is a legitimate goal.

packages.stem: A 62-year-old man is brought to the emergency department one hour after falling down a flight of stairs and striking his head. Bystanders report he was unresponsive for about a minute. He takes an oral anticoagulant for atrial fibrillation. His airway is clear, breathing is unlaboured and circulation is stable. He is drowsy but rousable, repeatedly asks the same questions, and has a boggy right parietal haematoma. Pupils are equal and reactive and there is no focal limb weakness.
packages.topic: Approach to Head Computed Tomography and Modality Selection by Neurologic Presentation

answer_choices: Start a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor and review the response
Start clonazepam as ongoing maintenance treatment
Prescribe lorazepam to be taken before anticipated stressful situations as her only ongoing treatment
Start zopiclone at night and treat the anxiety only if her sleep does not improve
Prescribe propranolol as her only ongoing treatment
packages.author_proposed_key: Start a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor and review the response
packages.author_rationale: Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors and serotonin-noradrenaline reuptake inhibitors are effective first-line pharmacotherapy for generalized anxiety disorder, while benzodiazepines should be kept brief because of dependence risk. Cognitive behavioural therapy is the first-choice psychological treatment and was appropriately offered; the patient's informed declining of it moves the decision to the first-line drug class rather than to a second-line or symptomatic agent. The learner should recognise that the presence of a first-line pharmacological option means the correct response to a declined psychotherapy is not a sedative or a symptomatic agent.

canadian_source_refs.organization: Centre for Addiction and Mental Health

packages.conditional_next_action_information: Had she accepted psychological treatment, cognitive behavioural therapy would be the first-choice psychological option, and a serotonin-noradrenaline reuptake inhibitor is an equally first-line pharmacological alternative to a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor. This item does not turn on a specific agent, dose or titration interval.
packages.lead_in: Which is the most appropriate initial pharmacological management?

per_distractor_rationales.choice: Start clonazepam as ongoing maintenance treatment
per_distractor_rationales.what_would_make_correct: Brief benzodiazepine use can have a place for short-term relief alongside a first-line treatment, not as the maintenance treatment itself.
per_distractor_rationales.why_inferior_here: Benzodiazepine use should be brief because of dependence risk, so making one the ongoing maintenance treatment for a chronic disorder is the wrong plan even though it would work in the short term.
per_distractor_rationales.why_plausible: Benzodiazepines relieve anxiety quickly and reliably, which makes them tempting as a maintenance treatment in a distressed and impaired patient.

per_distractor_rationales.choice: Prescribe lorazepam to be taken before anticipated stressful situations as her only ongoing treatment
per_distractor_rationales.what_would_make_correct: Short-term use in a defined, time-limited situation alongside first-line treatment is different from designating it the sole ongoing therapy.
per_distractor_rationales.why_inferior_here: It is still ongoing benzodiazepine treatment, which should be kept brief, and as her sole treatment it leaves the persistent generalised worry that defines her disorder untreated.
per_distractor_rationales.why_plausible: Intermittent rather than daily dosing appears to sidestep the dependence problem while still covering her worst moments.

per_distractor_rationales.choice: Start zopiclone at night and treat the anxiety only if her sleep does not improve
per_distractor_rationales.what_would_make_correct: Targeted treatment of a distinct primary sleep disorder would be appropriate, alongside rather than instead of first-line treatment of the anxiety disorder.
per_distractor_rationales.why_inferior_here: A hypnotic treats a symptom of the disorder rather than the disorder, and deferring first-line treatment until sleep fails to improve delays effective therapy in a patient whose function is already impaired.
per_distractor_rationales.why_plausible: Disturbed sleep is prominent in her presentation and improving it would plausibly improve the daytime symptoms.

per_distractor_rationales.choice: Prescribe propranolol as her only ongoing treatment
per_distractor_rationales.what_would_make_correct: It has a role in discrete performance-related autonomic symptoms, which is a different clinical problem from generalized anxiety disorder.
per_distractor_rationales.why_inferior_here: It addresses peripheral autonomic symptoms rather than the persistent cognitive worry that defines generalized anxiety disorder, and it is not the first-line pharmacotherapy for the condition.
per_distractor_rationales.why_plausible: Beta blockers blunt palpitations and tremor and are familiar to students as anxiety medications.

packages.stem: A 29-year-old woman has had ten months of excessive, difficult-to-control worry about her work, finances and her family's health, with restlessness, fatigue, poor concentration, irritability and disturbed sleep. She is missing deadlines and has stopped meeting friends. She drinks little alcohol, uses no other substances, has no depressive episode and no suicidal ideation, and physical examination and screening bloodwork are normal. A diagnosis of generalized anxiety disorder is made. Cognitive behavioural therapy is offered and discussed; she declines psychological treatment for now and asks to start a medication.

answer_choices: Explain that a daily benzodiazepine is not the first-line ongoing treatment, and recommend starting an antidepressant of the serotonin reuptake inhibitor class at a low dose, cautioning that anxiety can increase transiently before it improves.
Agree to continue the lorazepam indefinitely as his main ongoing treatment and add nothing further.
Recommend starting the antidepressant at a full therapeutic dose immediately, so that the benefit begins as quickly as possible.
Explain that medication has no role in panic disorder and that the attacks will settle on their own with time.
Explain that benzodiazepines are unsafe in panic disorder and must never be used at all.
packages.author_proposed_key: Explain that a daily benzodiazepine is not the first-line ongoing treatment, and recommend starting an antidepressant of the serotonin reuptake inhibitor class at a low dose, cautioning that anxiety can increase transiently before it improves.
packages.author_rationale: Two things must be communicated together. Serotonin reuptake inhibitors are the first-line medication option in panic disorder, and they should be started cautiously because early activation can transiently worsen anxiety, which is exactly the effect that drives patients back to a fast-acting benzodiazepine. Benzodiazepine treatment should be kept brief because of dependence risk, so it is not the ongoing plan. The learner should recognise that the speed of relief a patient reports is not the criterion for selecting maintenance treatment, and that warning the patient about early activation is what makes the first-line recommendation stick.

canadian_source_refs.organization: Centre for Addiction and Mental Health

packages.conditional_next_action_information: Cognitive behavioural therapy is a first-choice psychological treatment and would be offered alongside or instead of medication according to his preference and availability. This item does not turn on any specific agent, starting dose or titration interval.
packages.learner_decision: Counsel that benzodiazepines are not first-line for chronic management.

per_distractor_rationales.choice: Agree to continue the lorazepam indefinitely as his main ongoing treatment and add nothing further.
per_distractor_rationales.what_would_make_correct: Brief, time-limited use alongside a first-line treatment is different from indefinite monotherapy.
per_distractor_rationales.why_inferior_here: Benzodiazepine use should be brief because of dependence risk, so indefinite use as the main treatment is the plan the guidance specifically advises against, and it leaves the first-line option unoffered.
per_distractor_rationales.why_plausible: It respects the patient's stated preference and he reports genuine, rapid benefit.

per_distractor_rationales.choice: Recommend starting the antidepressant at a full therapeutic dose immediately, so that the benefit begins as quickly as possible.
per_distractor_rationales.what_would_make_correct: Reaching a full therapeutic dose is appropriate by gradual upward titration after a cautious start.
per_distractor_rationales.why_inferior_here: These medications should be started cautiously in panic disorder precisely to limit the early activation that can worsen anxiety; a full starting dose makes that activation more likely and risks the patient abandoning the treatment.
per_distractor_rationales.why_plausible: The drug class is correct and reaching an effective dose sooner appears to shorten his suffering.

per_distractor_rationales.choice: Explain that medication has no role in panic disorder and that the attacks will settle on their own with time.
per_distractor_rationales.what_would_make_correct: Nothing in this scenario; a patient choosing psychological treatment instead would be a different conversation, not a claim that medication has no role.
per_distractor_rationales.why_inferior_here: Effective first-line medication options exist for panic disorder, so telling a patient with six months of attacks and growing avoidance that medication has no role withholds an appropriate treatment.
per_distractor_rationales.why_plausible: Panic attacks are self-limiting events, and some patients do improve without medication.

per_distractor_rationales.choice: Explain that benzodiazepines are unsafe in panic disorder and must never be used at all.
per_distractor_rationales.what_would_make_correct: Nothing in this scenario; the accurate message is that their use should be brief, not that they are never used.
per_distractor_rationales.why_inferior_here: The guidance limits benzodiazepines to brief use rather than prohibiting them, so an absolute prohibition overstates the position and may damage the patient's trust when he learns otherwise.
per_distractor_rationales.why_plausible: It reaches the right conclusion about his ongoing treatment and sounds appropriately cautious.

packages.stem: A 34-year-old man has had six months of recurrent unexpected panic attacks with palpitations, breathlessness and a fear of dying, persistent worry about further attacks, and increasing avoidance of public transport. Cardiac and thyroid investigations were normal and panic disorder has been diagnosed. Two weeks ago a walk-in clinic gave him a short supply of lorazepam. He tells his family physician that it works within minutes and asks to stay on it as his ongoing treatment.

answer_choices: Carry out a suicide risk assessment now and arrange urgent care to establish his safety before other treatment proceeds
Refer him for trauma-focused psychotherapy at the next available appointment
Start a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor and review him in four weeks
Give advice on sleep and nightmares and review him in three months
Refer him for a non-urgent outpatient psychiatry assessment
packages.author_proposed_key: Carry out a suicide risk assessment now and arrange urgent care to establish his safety before other treatment proceeds
packages.author_rationale: Care in post-traumatic stress disorder begins with safety assessment, and evidence-based trauma-focused psychotherapies are the first-line treatments that follow it. This patient has disclosed current suicidal ideation with a formulated plan and access to means, which is the presentation that converts a routine treatment-planning visit into an urgent safety problem. The learner should recognise that the ordering is not negotiable: an appropriate first-line treatment delivered on a routine timeline is the wrong answer when safety has not been established, because it leaves the patient at risk during the interval.
packages.conditional_next_action_information: The result of the risk assessment determines the form urgent care takes, which may range from a same-day safety plan with intensified follow-up and removal of means to emergency department assessment or admission. Once safety is established, trauma-focused psychotherapy is the first-line treatment to plan.
packages.lead_in: Which is the most appropriate immediate next step?

per_distractor_rationales.choice: Refer him for trauma-focused psychotherapy at the next available appointment
per_distractor_rationales.what_would_make_correct: It becomes the right next step once safety has been assessed and addressed and the patient is being planned for definitive treatment.
per_distractor_rationales.why_inferior_here: Safety assessment precedes treatment in post-traumatic stress disorder, and a future appointment does nothing about a plan and means available tonight.
per_distractor_rationales.why_plausible: Trauma-focused psychotherapy is genuinely the first-line treatment for post-traumatic stress disorder and he came to discuss treatment.

per_distractor_rationales.choice: Start a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor and review him in four weeks
per_distractor_rationales.what_would_make_correct: Pharmacological treatment is reasonable as part of a longer-term plan established after safety has been addressed.
per_distractor_rationales.why_inferior_here: A four-week review interval leaves an acutely suicidal patient unsupervised, and starting a drug does not discharge the safety assessment that care begins with.
per_distractor_rationales.why_plausible: Medication has a role in post-traumatic stress disorder and starting something feels like active management.

per_distractor_rationales.choice: Give advice on sleep and nightmares and review him in three months
per_distractor_rationales.what_would_make_correct: Symptom-directed advice is reasonable in routine follow-up for a patient whose safety has been established.
per_distractor_rationales.why_inferior_here: It addresses a symptom while ignoring the disclosure of a suicidal plan with means, and a three-month interval is grossly inappropriate for an urgent safety concern.
per_distractor_rationales.why_plausible: Nightmares are prominent in his presentation and are a legitimate treatment target.

per_distractor_rationales.choice: Refer him for a non-urgent outpatient psychiatry assessment
per_distractor_rationales.what_would_make_correct: A non-urgent referral is appropriate for a patient without acute risk who needs specialist treatment planning.
per_distractor_rationales.why_inferior_here: Choosing the non-urgent pathway misclassifies the acuity; his disclosure requires assessment and arrangement of care now rather than a place on a routine waiting list.
per_distractor_rationales.why_plausible: Specialist psychiatric input is appropriate for complex post-traumatic stress disorder and a referral looks like escalation.

packages.stem: A 41-year-old man has post-traumatic stress disorder following a motor vehicle collision a year ago, with nightmares, intrusive memories, hypervigilance and avoidance of driving. He attends a scheduled family practice appointment to discuss treatment. During the visit he says that for the past week he has been thinking about ending his life, that he has worked out how he would do it, that he has the means at home, and that he does not think he can go on.

answer_choices: Offer the patient time alone, explain to both of them what will be kept confidential and the circumstances in which the physician would have to disclose, and assess the patient's capacity for the specific decisions at hand
Decline to see the patient alone at any point in the visit, on the basis that a patient under the age of 16 must always be seen with a parent present
See the patient alone for part of the visit, but agree in advance with the mother that the content of that private conversation will be reported back to her in full
Assure the patient, before the private part of the visit begins, that nothing she says will ever be disclosed to her mother or to anyone else under any circumstances
Defer any confidential discussion, and any assessment of her capacity to make her own decisions, until the patient reaches the age of 18
packages.author_proposed_key: Offer the patient time alone, explain to both of them what will be kept confidential and the circumstances in which the physician would have to disclose, and assess the patient's capacity for the specific decisions at hand
packages.author_rationale: Adolescent care should include private time with the patient, a clear explanation of the limits of confidentiality, and a case-specific assessment of capacity rather than a decision made on age alone. All three elements are needed together: private time without an explanation of limits promises more than can be delivered, and an explanation without private time does not create the conditions in which an adolescent will disclose. The learner should recognise that confidentiality in adolescent care is bounded rather than absolute, and that the boundaries are set out in advance to both the young person and the parent rather than discovered at the moment disclosure becomes necessary.

canadian_source_refs.locator: Recommendations; capacity and limits of confidentiality
canadian_source_refs.organization: Privacy and confidentiality in adolescent health care

packages.conditional_next_action_information: The specific circumstances in which disclosure is required, and the way capacity is documented, are shaped by the legislation and regulator expectations of the province or territory in which the physician practises; the elements described in the key are common to appropriate adolescent care across Canada.
packages.lead_in: Which response best reflects appropriate practice?

per_distractor_rationales.choice: Decline to see the patient alone at any point in the visit, on the basis that a patient under the age of 16 must always be seen with a parent present
per_distractor_rationales.what_would_make_correct: Nothing in this scenario; a patient who lacks capacity for a particular decision is managed with appropriate involvement of a substitute decision-maker, which is a capacity finding rather than an age rule.
per_distractor_rationales.why_inferior_here: Capacity is assessed case by case for the specific decision rather than by an age-only rule, and private time is part of appropriate adolescent care, so refusing it on age grounds is wrong.
per_distractor_rationales.why_plausible: Parents are ordinarily involved in a younger adolescent's care, and a fixed age cut-off appears to give a clear and defensible rule.

per_distractor_rationales.choice: See the patient alone for part of the visit, but agree in advance with the mother that the content of that private conversation will be reported back to her in full
per_distractor_rationales.what_would_make_correct: Sharing information with a parent is appropriate with the patient's agreement, or when a stated limit on confidentiality is reached.
per_distractor_rationales.why_inferior_here: Undertaking in advance to report everything empties the private time of its purpose and contradicts the confidentiality the adolescent must be able to rely on within its stated limits.
per_distractor_rationales.why_plausible: It appears to satisfy both parties and keeps the parent engaged in the adolescent's care.

per_distractor_rationales.choice: Assure the patient, before the private part of the visit begins, that nothing she says will ever be disclosed to her mother or to anyone else under any circumstances
per_distractor_rationales.what_would_make_correct: Nothing in this scenario; the correct assurance is specific about what is confidential and about the circumstances in which disclosure would be required.
per_distractor_rationales.why_inferior_here: Confidentiality has limits and those limits must be explained clearly; promising absolute secrecy is a commitment that cannot be honoured and that will be broken at the worst possible moment.
per_distractor_rationales.why_plausible: An unqualified promise is the most direct way to build trust and encourage an adolescent to speak freely.

per_distractor_rationales.choice: Defer any confidential discussion, and any assessment of her capacity to make her own decisions, until the patient reaches the age of 18
per_distractor_rationales.what_would_make_correct: Nothing in this scenario; the age of majority governs other matters but does not determine whether an adolescent receives private time or a capacity assessment.
per_distractor_rationales.why_inferior_here: It is the same age-only reasoning that guidance rejects, and it postpones by three years a conversation this patient needs at this visit.
per_distractor_rationales.why_plausible: The age of majority is a familiar bright line for independent decision-making.

packages.stem: A 15-year-old attends a family practice appointment with her mother because of three months of fatigue. She answers questions briefly and looks at her mother before each reply. When the physician suggests spending part of the visit with the patient alone, the mother objects and says that as the parent she expects to be told everything her daughter says.
